item.title: Nation to revamp train numbering system
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
Nation to revamp train numbering system China will overhaul its train numbering system to accommodate the expansion of its railway network, changing the meaning of several familiar letter prefixes while keeping routes and schedules unchanged under the current timetable. The changes, to be introduced in late November and late December, will increase the number of available train numbers for bullet train services by nearly 40 percent, China State Railway Group, the national railway operator, said on Friday. For travelers, including international visitors, the key change is that letters long associated with one type of train will identify another. T and K, previously used for regular speed express and fast trains, will identify high-speed services with top operating speeds of 300 kilometers per hour and 200 to 250 km/h, respectively. G will identify Fuxing trains with a maximum operating speed of 350 km/h. The X prefix will be reserved for Fuxing trains operating above 350 km/h. However, no X series passenger services will begin operating in this round of changes, said Xu Yan, deputy director of the operator's passenger transport center. The overhaul follows substantial growth in railway services. Between 2014 and 2025, China's railway network expanded from 112,000 kilometers to 165,000 km, while the average number of passenger trains operating daily rose from 4,894 to 11,796. "During peak travel periods such as the May Day and National Day holidays, G series services use more than 90 percent of the available train numbers for that prefix," said Fan Mingxiang, deputy director of the operator's transport department. Wei Yuguang, a professor at Beijing Jiaotong University, said train numbers serve purposes far beyond helping passengers find their trains. "They are a common language for coordination across regions and departments," he said, explaining that each train's unique number is a basic unit for organizing transport, dispatching, passenger services and accounting. Even the length of a number matters. "Using three digits or four may mean just one extra word each time for a dispatcher, but repeated throughout the day, it adds considerably to the workload," Wei said. Pronunciation also needs to be considered. "If two train numbers sound very similar, that can cause problems in dispatching," he said. Wei said the new system builds on existing rules while making room for more trains and new services. It must accommodate both passenger and freight trains, including those operating across borders. Cross-border passenger services will also have their train numbers adjusted on domestic sections of their routes under the revised rules, the operator said. Regular speed passenger trains, tourist trains and some freight services will have their numbers changed in late November, followed by high-speed and other services in late December. The new train numbers will appear on 12306, China's official railway booking platform, when tickets go on sale, up to 15 days before departure. Onboard services, including quiet carriages and online meal ordering, will remain unchanged. For international visitors who rely on travel guides to plan their trips, older explanations of train prefixes may no longer apply after the changes. The operator urged passengers to check train numbers, departure and arrival stations, and schedules carefully.

item.title: Shanghai prepares for 9th CIIE
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
Shanghai prepares for 9th CIIE Exhibition area of the expo to exceed 440,000 square meters for first time The upcoming 9th China International Import Expo represents a major effort by the world's second-largest economy to proactively open its super-sized market to the world, officials and executives said ahead of the event, which is scheduled to take place Nov 5 to 10 in Shanghai. With its total exhibition area set to exceed 440,000 square meters for the first time, this year's expo will host 4,142 overseas exhibitors and draw participants from 162 countries, regions and international organizations, said Yan Dong, vice-minister of commerce, at a news conference on Friday. "US companies will occupy more than 50,000 sq m at the business exhibition, up 1,500 sq m from last year, retaining the top spot by exhibition area for the eighth consecutive year," Yan said. Having never missed an edition of the CIIE, US technology company 3M will showcase its latest innovations in automotive, electronics and safety, as well as manufacturing materials and automation. "We have always viewed the CIIE as a key platform for showcasing cutting-edge innovations and expanding local partnerships," said Henry Ding, president of 3M China, adding that the company will further strengthen its supply chain network in China. Such confidence is backed by the returns foreign-invested companies earn in China. Foreign-invested companies that filed annual reports for 2025 recorded an average profit margin of 8.7 percent, according to a report released by the Ministry of Commerce. Foreign-invested manufacturers posted a margin 2.2 percentage points higher than that of industrial enterprises nationwide, the report said. "China's super-sized market offers fertile ground for businesses to generate tangible returns," said He Yadong, a spokesman for the ministry, at a separate news conference on Thursday. In addition to connecting global businesses with China's vast market, the expo is also cementing its role as a showcase for innovation. Yan, the commerce official, said the number of exhibits set to make their global, Asian or China debuts has so far exceeded 480, a record high for the event. The lineup will include modular laparoscopic surgical robots, cochlear implants that detect sound from all directions and prototype 6G devices, said Xiao Lu, deputy Party secretary of the China International Import Expo Bureau. "These cutting-edge innovations will support industrial development and improve people's lives," Xiao said, adding that other exhibits will include water-based silicone pressure-sensitive adhesives and water treatment systems that can soften and mineralize water simultaneously. The expo comes as strong import growth lends support to Beijing's push for more balanced trade. China's imports rose 22.3 percent year-on-year to 16.74 trillion yuan ($2.5 trillion) in the first nine months, the fastest growth since 2021, according to the General Administration of Customs. Shanghai, the expo's host city, saw imports reach a record 1.87 trillion yuan in the first eight months, accounting for 12.8 percent of the national total, said Lu Shan, the city's vice-mayor. Yan said China will respond proactively to trading partners' needs and continue to improve measures to facilitate imports. "We will work to enable the world to share in the opportunities of China's vast market," he added.

item.title: Nation strengthening global outreach of TCM
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
Nation strengthening global outreach of TCM Traditional Chinese medicine is accelerating its global outreach, with the value and benefits of TCM gaining broader recognition worldwide, as China continues to step up international cooperation — from organizing training programs to sending medical teams overseas. TCM has reached 196 countries and regions worldwide, according to the National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine. China has signed TCM cooperation agreements with nearly 50 foreign governments, regional authorities and international organizations, and has set up 30 high-quality overseas TCM centers and 31 national-level TCM service export facilities, the administration said. These centers and facilities conduct medical services, personnel training, scientific research and cultural exchanges in countries involved in the Belt and Road Initiative, it added. The administration released the information ahead of the two-day World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026, which is scheduled to open on Saturday in Beijing. The theme for this year's conference is "Technology Empowerment and Integrated Development: Advancing Traditional Medicine for All". At a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday, President Xi Jinping said that China has established the world's largest traditional medicine service system, as well as the world's largest system for medical service, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security. He called for efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of TCM and to strengthen the coordinated and integrated development of TCM and Western medicine. In a congratulatory letter sent to the inaugural edition of the conference, which was held in December 2024 in Beijing, Xi had reaffirmed China's commitment to enhancing traditional medicine to better benefit people around the world. China is willing to work with the international community to foster mutual learning in traditional medicine, integrate it more deeply into the global health system, and promote the innovative transformation and development of traditional medicine culture, Xi said in his message. Tangible benefits Amanda, a TCM practitioner from the United States, is among the many international students who have benefited from training programs held for foreigners at Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine in Jiangsu province. Guan Xiaowei, who organizes these training programs, said that earlier Amanda used to hesitate before inserting an acupuncture needle into a patient, worried that it might hurt. "Amanda overcame her hesitation after she witnessed how widely TCM is accepted among the people in China. She told me that she could now return home with much more confidence in her practice," Guan added. In recent years, a growing number of students, medical practitioners and TCM enthusiasts from the US have traveled to China to gain a deeper understanding of traditional remedies and hone their practical skills. "Some have personally benefited from acupuncture and other TCM therapies, or have relatives and friends who have; so they came here seeking to understand better the science behind it," Guan said. "Some are also health professionals who wish to expand their skills amid the growing popularity of TCM and integrative medicine in the US," she added. Furthermore, cultural curiosity is driving the popularity of TCM, Guan noted. "There are many people interested in kung fu or tai chi, and they want to explore the TCM principles behind these, such as the balance of yin and yang and the harmony between humans and nature," she said. According to the TCM administration, China has sent TCM teams in five batches to Cambodia as part of broader efforts to deliver tangible benefits to more people. The China-Cambodia Traditional Chinese Medicine Center in Phnom Penh, the Cambodian capital, now receives about 10,000 medical visits each year, more than half of them from Cambodians or other non-Chinese patients. The center also sends TCM practitioners to remote and rural areas about twice each month, and has trained two local nurses. Cooperation mechanisms China has launched an initiative called New Era Shennong Tasting Herbs, promoting international cooperation in research and application of traditional medicinal resources. Under the initiative, the TCM administration has signed cooperation agreements with Indonesia and Seychelles, and supported the establishment of interagency cooperation mechanisms with more than 10 countries to carry out joint research on medicinal resources. Meanwhile, the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry was set up by the China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences and other institutions, in order to advance the quality of clinical studies and standardized development. China has also facilitated the establishment of a technical committee dedicated to traditional medicine within the International Organization for Standardization and has contributed to the release of 147 international standards for TCM. The administration said it is committed to promoting high-quality TCM services overseas and deepening cooperation with the World Health Organization and other international agencies and countries in the future. Efforts will also be made to step up the development of overseas TCM centers and promote policy communication and regulatory alignment in areas such as the registration of TCM products and the application of standards, while strengthening evidence-based research, innovation and the development of international standards, according to the administration. Guo Jun contributed to this story.

item.title: Xi: Prioritize ecological conservation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Xi: Prioritize ecological conservation He stresses green development on Inner Mongolia inspection tour President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to coordinate high-quality development with high-level protection of the environment, and underlined the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks on Friday during an inspection tour in Ulaanqab, Inner Mongolia autonomous region. Noting that green development is an essential aspect of high-quality growth, he urged a holistic approach to the conservation of mountains, rivers, forests, farmlands, lakes, grasslands and deserts, and called for efforts to promote carbon reduction, pollution reduction, green expansion and growth in a coordinated manner. Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he heard reports on the autonomous region's efforts to strengthen local ecological conservation, particularly enhance environmental governance and restore the ecosystem of Huangqihai Lake, an inland lake that was once on the verge of drying up due to climatic and other factors. He underlined the need to protect the wetlands, with focus on enhancing the quality and stability of ecosystems while maintaining biodiversity. With abundant wind and solar resources, Ulaanqab has leveraged its advantages in terms of location, climate and green electricity to develop the green computing industry, achieving significant progress. In the Qahar High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Xi learned about the progress of the "East Data, West Computing" project, a megaproject that aims to coordinate the computing capabilities of the country's eastern regions with inland western regions, as well as the development of green computing in Inner Mongolia. He pointed out that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building an integrated national computing network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee. Xi emphasized the need to strengthen scientific planning, resources support and security assurance to ensure that existing projects are operated in an efficient manner and that projects still under construction are completed as scheduled. Efforts should be made to extend the industrial chain and promote the deep integration of the digital economy with the real economy, continuously transforming the strength in computing into development advantages, he said. While interacting with project leaders, technicians and staff members of the development zone, Xi emphasized that the computing network is one of the "six networks" planned and constructed by the country, and it is in a stage of accelerated development with broad prospects. China is accelerating a sweeping infrastructure plan centered around "six networks" — water, power, computing, telecommunications, urban pipelines and logistics — in order to stabilize investment, create jobs and lay the groundwork for the next phase of the country's technological and industrial transformation. Highlighting the importance of "computing-electricity synergy" and "computing-water synergy", Xi encouraged them to ensure smooth construction and operation of computing center projects and play an active role in the development of green computing, thereby contributing more to the building of a digital China and promoting the development of new quality productive forces. In 2025, Inner Mongolia generated more than 270 billion kilowatt-hours of renewable power, ranking among the top regions nationwide. This clean energy provides a stable power supply for energy-intensive data centers. As of July this year, the autonomous region's total computing power reached 345,000 PFlops, a unit representing one quadrillion calculations per second. Notably, over 85 percent of the electricity used by regional data centers comes from green power. Inner Mongolia has developed a dual-hub strategy centered in Hohhot, the regional capital, and Ulaanqab. The two centers operate in synergy and complement each other, efficiently handling high-intensity artificial intelligence computing tasks for both industrial and public sectors. During his tour, Xi also inspected local distinctive agricultural and livestock products, and encouraged the region to strengthen links between production and sales to increase incomes for local farmers and herdsmen. He emphasized that China is vast, with significant differences in resource endowments across its various regions. All regions should build on their respective conditions, leverage their comparative advantages, and pursue high-quality development tailored to local circumstances, he said. Xi's last inspection trip to Inner Mongolia was in June 2023. During that tour, he had urged the autonomous region to consolidate its role as a vital ecological barrier in northern China — the country's important base for energy and strategic resources, its important production base for agricultural commodities and livestock, and a vital gateway for opening-up to countries and regions north of China.

item.title: New guidelines issued to regulate nursing home costs
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
New guidelines issued to regulate nursing home costs The central government has published guidelines to regulate the pricing policies of elderly nursing homes in order to let seniors get affordable, qualified and sustainable services. The guidelines are jointly unveiled by the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the National Health Commission. The guidelines clarify that nursing homes' pricing policies cover basic fees for beds and services, extra fees for diets and fees for on-demand home services. The government-sponsored nursing homes follow government-guided prices, and their pricing policies should be set by provincial-level departments or authorized city-level authorities. Commercial nursing homes are encouraged to offer high-quality services with favorable prices based on their running costs and people's demands, according to the guidelines. The guidelines have urged local authorities to optimize standards and evaluation mechanisms for nursing homes' pricing policies to make sure these policies are reasonable and transparent. For example, the pricing policies should be based on people's disposable incomes and the area's human resources costs. Also, the guidelines urge local authorities to improve guidance to nursing home operators and help them not only provide better services for the elderly, but also to prevent possible risks and settle disputes. Local authorities should cooperate closely with each other to crack down on improper or illegal behaviors such as not implementing government-guided prices or not marking prices clearly to secure the rights of seniors. As of the end of 2025, China had about 395,000 nursing homes and facilities nationwide with 7.68 million beds for the elderly, according to the civil affairs ministry.

item.title: Cook says China is key to iPhone Duo's success
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Cook says China is key to iPhone Duo's success Apple's first foldable smartphone is manufactured exclusively in China and Chinese app developers are crucial to iPhone Duo's success, Tim Cook, Apple's executive chairman, said in a recent exclusive interview with China Daily in Beijing. The remarks underline the great importance of China to United States tech companies such as Apple, as China is not just a huge market, but also an innovation center and a key manufacturing hub for their global operations, experts said. Cook said Chinese developers' enthusiasm for the foldable device and China's manufacturing capabilities are part of the recipe behind iPhone Duo's success. "We are working with a number of developers and optimizing some of the things at (our) Shanghai developer center. The apps are extremely important to us, and we're helping hand in hand," he said, adding that Chinese developers play a critical role in that process and they're very innovative. "China's market for foldables is second to none," Cook added. As Apple's first foldable model, iPhone Duo is far more difficult to manufacture than previous products. According to Apple, the process requires strong manufacturing precision and design capabilities, and it manages that through close collaboration with suppliers. Bai Ming, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation, said, "China's decades of experience in electronics manufacturing and its continued push to pursue advanced and smart manufacturing make it the only country capable of making complicated products such as iPhone Duo." Cook is on a multi-stop visit to China, touring cities including Guangzhou in Guangdong province, Beijing and Shanghai. On Friday, Cook said at a forum in Shanghai that China's artificial intelligence application landscape is showing unprecedented dynamism, and AI is already having a profound impact on Apple's supply chain. During the trip, the senior executive also said that Apple Intelligence — which incorporates Chinese tech company Alibaba's Qwen large language model — has received approval in China and a test version is set to launch later this month. On Thursday, Commerce Minister Wang Wentao met Cook in Beijing, where they exchanged views on issues including China-US economic and trade relations. Notably, Cook said that Apple will further expand its business in China. Cook's visit came amid a wave of top US business executives' recent visits to China. Ray Dalio, founder of Bridgewater Associates, also visited Beijing this week. Sean Stein, president of the US-China Business Council, said the planet's most innovative companies are concentrated in the US and China, which lays a solid foundation for wider cooperation. "Such collaboration stretches well beyond one, two or even three industries — a reflection of a deliberate effort by firms on both sides to learn from each other and forge partnerships across the globe," Stein said. According to a report released by the American Chamber of Commerce in South China earlier this year, 75 percent of enterprises it surveyed plan to reinvest in China in 2026, and over the next three to five years, its member companies are expected to reinvest $13.79 billion in profits generated in China. Gong Yu, founder and CEO of Chinese video-streaming company iQiyi — which Cook visited during his trip — said the ties between the two companies can be dated back to 2010. "Innovation in hardware, including the application of AI technology, has given us a particularly good synergy. This kind of mechanism allows us to achieve one plus one bigger than two, enabling this synergy to unleash even greater value," Gong said.

item.title: Revolutionary spirit lives on in a new generation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Revolutionary spirit lives on in a new generation Ninety years after victory in the Long March, officers carry its legacy forward A pair of scissors snips carefully through a sheet of red paper. With a few precise cuts, the silhouette of a Red Army soldier takes shape. It is a tactile echo of a journey that took place some 90 years ago. In Huining, in Northwest China's Gansu province, history is never a distant abstraction. It is woven into the daily rhythm of soldiers like Xin Kaixuan, an officer in the Baiyin detachment of the People's Armed Police Force who leads a paper-cutting group with his comrades. For Xin, crafting figures of revolutionary veterans isn't just about preserving folk art; it is a way to bridge the gap between past endurance and present duty. Xin, who has loved paper-cutting since childhood, began creating works depicting Red Army soldiers and scenes from the Long March after joining his unit eight years ago. "Through paper-cutting, we can learn about the history of the Long March while passing on traditional culture in Huining," he said. "We also have calligraphy and reading groups, which give us more opportunities to learn about our history and culture." Ninety years ago in October 1936, the First, Second and Fourth Front armies of the Red Army converged right here in Huining, sealing the victory of the Long March. Today, a new generation of soldiers faces a different kind of march: not across freezing snow mountains, but through the quiet, demanding grind of modern service, community building and safeguarding a changing land.

item.title: Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary BEIJING -- President Xi Jinping on Friday extended congratulations to faculty, students and alumni of Hunan University as it marks its 100th anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a congratulatory letter to the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward fine revolutionary traditions, continue to elevate the quality and levels of its teaching, and strive to nurture more talent who can apply their knowledge to practical affairs, so as to make new contributions to building China into an education powerhouse and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1926, Hunan University has nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent over the past century.
